title: LSU announces final decision on adding former NFL players
description: The biggest storyline in college football over the past few weeks has been LSU and head coach Lane Kiffin’s attempts to add multiple players to its roster who had signed NFL contracts and spent time with NFL teams this preseason. Now, LSU has made a final decision on that matter. With the looming threat of…
fullText:
The biggest storyline in college football over the past few weeks has been LSU and head coach Lane Kiffin's attempts to add multiple players to its roster who had signed NFL contracts and spent time with NFL teams this preseason. Now, LSU has made a final decision on that matter.

With the looming threat of expulsion from the SEC, the Tigers have made it clear that they will not add the players to the roster this season.

Heading into the 2026 season, LSU and Kiffin had been moving forward with plans to bring in at least three players who signed professional contracts this summer, including former Ole Miss players Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris.

Adding those players to the roster would break two separate league rules, as the SEC prohibits players from entering the conference after signing a professional contract while also restricting intraconference transfers outside of the designated transfer portal window.

However, a Baton Rouge judge has issued an order preventing both the NCAA and SEC from enforcing their restrictions related to eligibility, the transfer portal, and professional players returning to college football.

On Thursday last week, Judge William Jorden, out of Baton Rouge, Louisiana, ruled in favor of LSU by approving a preliminary injunction "that prohibits the NCAA and SEC from punishing any school" that fields former professional players. That would have paved the way for the players to potentially play in Saturday's game against Clemson.

Ultimately, LSU opted against adding the players to the roster for this game. However, the team only rostered 103 players for the game, allowing two open spots to potentially add Wright and Harris to the roster later in the season.

According to college football insider Pete Thamel of ESPN, LSU has announced a final decision on the matter by adding two additional players to the school's roster. This means that the team's roster is now full at 105 players, and Wright and Harris will not be able to be added to the roster this season.

"NEWS: LSU football is adding two players to the school's roster, which will complete it at 105 players, per ESPN sources. This will lock LSU's roster for the rest of the year, which will eliminate the program's ability to add Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris," Thamel wrote in a post on X.

This should seemingly bring the whole ordeal to a close.

title: LSU locks roster, Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris will not play for the Tigers
description: Wright and Harris were both on rosters during the NFL preseason, and their potential return to college football sparked plenty of controversy.
fullText:
The battle over former NFL players returning to college appears to be over, for now.

LSU has added two players to its roster, bringing the total to 105 players. The Tigers added DE Gabriel Reliford and CB Aidan Anding, per Yahoo Sports' Ross Dellenger.

With the roster at 105 players, neither Dae'Quan Wright nor Zxavian Harris will be allowed to join the LSU roster this season.

Wright and Harris have been in the media and the subject of plenty of discussion because both of them participated in this year's NFL preseason, going so far as to suit up for preseason games.

After not making their respective NFL rosters, and after the NCAA passed a new eligibility rule allowing players five years of eligibility over five years, both Wright and Harris were looking to return to the college ranks for one more season.

Lawyers got involved, and different injunctions were permitted in different states, and the situation got extremely confusing and murky very quickly.

This sparked plenty of controversy among FBS teams, culminating in the SEC and LSU scheduling court dates and meetings to discuss what could be done to the school should it add pro players. One outcome included the conference removing LSU as a member school, but that may have been avoided.

While this seems like it was a big threat from the SEC, Dellenger reported that if the vote had passed and been enacted immediately, next week's highly anticipated game between Ole Miss and LSU would have suddenly been a non-conference game.

At this time, it has not been reported whether Thursday's scheduled meeting to "decide whether to terminate Louisiana State University ('LSU') as an SEC member institution" has been canceled or if it will still be held.

Wright and Harris were ruled eligible ahead of LSU's season-opening game against Clemson. Both players were with new head coach Lane Kiffin at Ole Miss, but Kiffin opted not to add them to the roster at the time, leaving two spots open out of a maximum of 105.

The LSU head coach spoke about the decision during an appearance on "College GameDay," mainly attributing it to the fact that they didn't yet know what a punishment, if any, would look like for the program.

"That wasn't easy. As much as I feel for the players, and I believe that you fight for what you believe in, and I believe that, you know, these kids have an opportunity to play, just like all of the other kids around the country that are winning court cases and being put on rosters.

But the same time, I'm the head coach at LSU and I had to make a decision that is for the big picture of LSU and the LSU football program, with the uncertainties of what potentially could've come by adding them to the roster."

"That wasn't easy. As much as I feel for the players ... I had to make a decision that is for the big picture of LSU."

Lane Kiffin on the decision to not roster Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris for today's game against Clemson. pic.twitter.com/iPVHJTYoav

Now with its roster officially set, LSU will look to continue the momentum generated with a Week 1 dominant 51-10 win over Clemson.

title: Bears Rookie Gets Thrown Into the Fire in Week 1
description: Dillon Thieneman dreamed about his first NFL regular-season game as a kid. Now, the Chicago Bears rookie safety will get […]
fullText:
Dillon Thieneman dreamed about his first NFL regular-season game as a kid. Now, the Chicago Bears rookie safety will get there with far more on his shoulders than most first-year players could expect.

The Bears open their 2026 season Sunday against the Carolina Panthers needing Thieneman to be more than a promising young player. They need him to be steady. They need him to communicate. And, most of all, they need him to help eliminate the backbreaking explosive plays that undermined their defense in recent years.

That is a massive assignment for any rookie, particularly one walking into an unsettled safety room.

Chicago lost projected starter Coby Bryant to a major knee injury during training camp, and the team placed slot cornerback Kyler Gordon on the physically unable-to-perform list. Gordon must miss at least the first four games, potentially more. The Bears have veteran options in Xavier Woods and Cam Lewis alongside Thieneman, but neither uncertainty disappears simply because the regular season is here.

Thieneman, the rookie selected 25th overall in April, has become the constant.

That is not how the Bears envisioned their back end at the start of camp. But Thieneman handled the summer well enough that the team can reasonably expect him to play a major role immediately. His range, instinctiveness and willingness to tackle have shown up throughout camp and the preseason. His next challenge is preventing the mistakes that turn a good defensive call into a 40-yard gain.

Dillon Thieneman showing off the range to breakup this pass intended for Carnell Tate

Future perennial Pro Bowler pic.twitter.com/AFQ6eJrwaJ

Chicago's defense struggled to limit explosive plays last season, a weakness that puts more pressure on its reshaped safety group. That is not a problem one player can solve alone, but safeties are often the final line of defense when a coverage breaks down or a runner gets through the first two levels.

Thieneman knows the difference between merely understanding the system and playing quickly within it.

"I've got a better understanding of tendencies," he said Monday. "So now it's taking that next step and not only just knowing it, but being able to anticipate it and use it to your advantage."

That is the leap the Bears need him to make sooner rather than later.

Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen's scheme should help. Thieneman said the defense has structure and rules, but Allen does not want defenders frozen by the call sheet. He gives players room to communicate, adjust and trust what they see before the snap.

"I think it's pretty simple," Thieneman said. "Obviously, there's complexities within it, but a lot of times he makes a call and he lets people on the field just play football. … If we see it a little differently, he's like, 'You guys are out on the field. You guys call it.' That's been pretty cool."

That freedom is valuable, but it also demands maturity. A rookie safety can get himself into trouble by trying to make the perfect play rather than the correct one. Thieneman will have to balance his aggressive instincts with the discipline to stay on top of routes, make the proper checks and ensure everyone in the secondary sees the formation the same way.

The Bears did not leave him alone to figure that out. Thieneman has spent camp working alongside Lewis and Woods, two veterans with far more NFL experience. He said he feels comfortable with both players and regularly talks through what they saw on the field and the sideline.

"They definitely have a lot of experience able to help me," Thieneman said. "I've been talking to them a lot just in the meeting room, like how they see things. And out on the field, we'll talk once we're on the sideline. But I feel very comfortable and able to communicate and kind of anticipate what the other guys are thinking."

That comfort matters because Chicago could need all three players in different roles. Lewis has experience at safety and nickel cornerback. Woods brings physicality and has pushed for a starting job since signing late in camp. Rookie Malik Muhammad appears positioned to begin in the slot while Gordon is sidelined, but the Bears have options if they decide they need Lewis there instead.

The lineup may change. Thieneman's importance will not.

He has already received practical advice on handling the inevitable ups and downs of a rookie season. Assistant defensive backs coach Matt Giordano told him to learn from the bad moments without letting them linger.

"Just take it one day at a time," Thieneman said. "Something bad happens, learn from it, move on. Don't linger too long."

That philosophy will get tested quickly. The Panthers will look for every communication lapse and every inexperienced defender they can isolate. The Bears cannot bet on their rookie safety to be perfect in Week 1, but they need him to be poised.

Thieneman has waited a long time for this moment. The Bears are asking him to make the most of it immediately.

title: Week 1 Fantasy Football Injury Report: TreVeyon Henderson, George Kittle And More
description: The 2026 NFL season begins with Week 1 injury reports heavily influencing fantasy football decisions.
fullText:
At long last, the 2026 NFL season is about to begin. While there's still time to squeeze in a few final fantasy football drafts, managers are already having to parse injury reports as they make their lineup decisions for Week 1.

On Wednesday night, the reigning champion Seattle Seahawks will host the New England Patriots in a rematch of Super Bowl LX. The Patriots overhauled their receiving corps this offseason by adding AJ Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles and Romeo Doubs from the Green Bay Packers, but their skill-position corps could be down a key player against Seattle.

On Thursday, the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers will clash in Melbourne, Australia, with plenty of injury question marks on both sides. Fantasy managers did get some clarity on Monday about one veteran receiver, but uncertainty otherwise still abounds in this matchup.

The season kicks off in full on Sunday with 13 games on the docket. Teams playing Sunday don't have to submit their first injury report until Wednesday, so we won't get updates on a pair of key running backs until then. But we're already starting to get a steady trickle of updates hinting at who may—and may not—be available for Week 1.

Every Tuesday, we'll be breaking down the biggest injury news that could shape your fantasy football lineup for the upcoming week. Let's dive into all of the most notable updates ahead of Week 1.

New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson hasn't practiced since Aug. 24 because of an ankle injury, leaving his status for Week 1 up in the air. He missed practice Sunday and Monday, although the Patriots still haven't clarified his official status for Wednesday's season opener.

"We'll see how he feels today," Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters prior to Monday's practice. "We'll see if he can do anything. He's been working extremely hard to come back, and we'll see where that goes here today. We do have a few more days before (the game), but we'll just see what he can do today."

According to ESPN's Mike Reiss, veteran tailback Rhamondre Stevenson would be the Patriots' starter even if Henderson does play, in part because the Patriots appear to trust him 

Fantasy managers with Henderson on their rosters should be exploring backup plans. Even if he does get declared active, is it worth the risk of him playing sparingly against a potentially stingy Seattle defense?

Arizona Cardinals rookie running back Jeremiyah Love suffered a high ankle sprain during his first preseason game on Aug. 13 and hasn't practiced since. Last week, NFL Network's Mike Garafolo said he was "50/50" to play in the Cardinals' season opener against the Los Angeles Chargers.

However, Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters Monday that Love was "progressing" and "moving around" during the team's walkthrough. When asked about Love's chances of playing Sunday in the season opener, LaFleur replied, "I feel good."

Love piled up 11 carries for 58 yards and three catches for 14 yards against the Las Vegas Raiders in his lone preseason action, and he figures to be the focal point of the Cardinals' offense once he's back up to speed. It wouldn't be surprising if veteran tailback Tyler Allgeier siphoned off more work from Love in the red zone early on, though.

On Aug. 23, Vincent Bonsignore of the California Post briefly brought fantasy football managers to a halt when he reported Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty got hurt in practice and "could not put pressure on his leg when leaving the field." Thankfully, ESPN's Adam Schefter followed up later that night to add that Jeanty was "believed to have sprained his ankle" and it was "not considered a long-term injury."

According to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Jeanty's ankle sprain is "more low than high" and is "not considered to be a major injury." Last week, Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak told reporters that he was optimistic about Jeanty being available for the season opener against the Miami Dolphins.

Backup running back Mike Washington Jr. dazzled during the preseason and is worth picking up in leagues of all sizes just in case Jeanty does miss time or aggravate his injury. But for now, it sounds like Jeanty managers dodged a major bullet even if he does wind up missing Week 1.

Chicago Bears wide receiver Rome Odunze exited practice last Thursday after he "came up hobbling during an install period," according to Sean Hammond of the Chicago Tribune. "He wasn't overly concerned—he tried to stay in—but trainers pulled him off," Hammond added.

Dan Wiederer of The Athletic reported "preliminary indications" were that Odunze "should be all good" after leaving practice. However, Odunze was absent from the Bears' practice on Monday, according to ESPN's Courtney Cronin.

The Bears might just be limiting Odunze's reps early in the week with an eye on getting him as close to 100% for the season opener. But until he's back on the practice field, managers should at least keep an eye on whether he'll be available against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. If not, wide receiver Luther Burden III and tight end Colston Loveland should be busy in the passing game.

San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle suffered a torn Achilles tendon during his team's Wild Card Round win over the Philadelphia Eagles in January. Eight months later, he might already be back on the field.

On Tuesday in Australia (Monday in the U.S.), Niners offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak told reporters that Kittle is "looking like himself, looking fresh." He added that Kittle is "practicing full speed" and is "getting a ton of reps" before hedging with, "How that affects on him on game day and what the workload is will be determined."

The Niners figure to ease Kittle back into action and not give him his typical complement of snaps in Week 1 against the Los Angeles Rams. Fantasy managers with Kittle on their rosters should at least considered having a backup plan in place even if he does play, as he could get eased back into action slowly.

Like Odunze, D'Andre Swift also left practice this past Thursday in "significant discomfort," according to Schefter. However, he was "said to be experiencing a 'cramp,'" Schefter added, and was back on the field at practice Monday. Cronin wrote in late August that Swift "had arguably the best training camp of any offensive skill player" for the Bears, so he should be wheels up for Week 1 against the Panthers.

Mike Evans missed time during training camp with quadricep and adductor injuries, but he told reporters in Australia that none of them "were significant." He added that had it been a normal game week, he "wouldn't have missed any time." Until Kittle is back up to speed, Evans has a chance to be the top red-zone target for quarterback Brock Purdy. He should be in fantasy lineups as long as he's healthy.

Puka Nacua dealt with a psoas injury in training camp, but Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay expects him to play Thursday against the Niners. Schefter also told ESPN's Pat McAfee that there's "a real possibility" Nacua doesn't face any discipline this season even though he's being sued for assault and battery by a woman "who says he made an antisemitic mark and bit her on the shoulder on New Year's Eve," according to the Associated Press. If he's playing, you're starting him. Simple as that.

Alec Pierce underwent ankle surgery in March and just returned to practice for the first time on Aug. 27, but Indianapolis Colts head coach Shane Steichen told reporters Monday that Pierce is expected to suit up Sunday against the Baltimore Ravens. Colts quarterback Daniel Jones is on the mend from a torn Achilles, so it wouldn't be surprising if the offense—and Pierce in particular—got off to a slow start. He'd be a risky play in Week 1, but he has far higher upside than most of the players being drafted in his range.

title: Football-tangential things to look forward to during the 2026 NFL regular season
description: These are the things I love about football, beyond the actual football
fullText:
You're likely not reading this if you don't think football is awesome. The most casual of observers don't come to SB Nation sites and click on stories to read on a random weekday. Thus, I'm not telling you anything you don't already know. But it's not just the actual sport of football, played between whistles, that makes us love football so much. It's all the phenomena that are football-related that add to our enjoyment of the season that always seemed too short.

First, I would encourage you to share the non-football events, moments, or traditions that make the sport's 18+ weeks so much fun for you in the comments below (maybe someone can pick up an enjoyable idea). Secondly, I'll share some of mine here:

I strongly ascribe to the belief that traditional food calendars should not influence your culinary choices. If you want stew on a hot summer day, you should have it. If it's the dead of winter and you want some ice cream, get some ice cream. Whether it's a usually-prepared "summer food" or not should not stop you from enjoying it. When it's considered seasonally appropriate, who knows if it'll hit the spot then? I will not be oppressed by the tyranny of the fictitious food calendar!

That being said, certain people and restaurants do not ascribe to my progressive culinary thinking. Because of that, my food options are sometimes slightly limited by what the person or establishment deems appropriate for the season, and that exclusion stops now. If I was a pumpkin spice person like my wife (to complete the ensemble with the Ugg boots and leggings), I'd be blocked off from getting it until the Starbucks overlords deemed appropriate to bless the peasants with that overly-nutmegged (that's totally a word) liquid concoction. So I'm excited for the new wing flavors. I'm excited for all the caramel apple desserts. I'm excited for my local shop to start offering their pumpkin rolls again.

As long as I'm forced to live in a society that doesn't let me have the easiest access to apple fritters in June, I'll be grateful for the return of some elite-tier foods.

Much like my above take on food, I'm a "wear what you want, when you want"-kind of guy…

…but you know, the weather and stuff.

As long as you live in the Northern Hemisphere, fall and winter are cooler than summer. How much cooler depends on your location, but for a lot of people, American football season (and the immediate aftermath) is the only time they can wear a hooded sweatshirt outside their house without it quickly serving as an inadvertent sauna suit. The joy of this article of clothing is also related to the first point identified above, as the magic of the hoodie allows for a few extra fall pounds to be packed onto a human body secretly, well hidden by the sweatshirt until which time as the spring comes and we begin to slightly regret our football-related consumption choices.

Maybe the Bills should play Josh Allen at linebacker.

Maybe Aaron Kromer should have been made the head coach.

Win or lose, the people who call into stations like WGR 550 or 97 Rock (the new Buffalo Bills flagship station) immediately post-game can provide some of the most unhinged and galaxy-brained ideas and takes that anyone sober could ever truly appreciate. No matter what you believe to be the most relevant issues surrounding the team after a regular season or playoff game, the hard left and right turns provided to you by some of the individuals who call into the post-game radio shows make the programs must-listen simply for the entertainment value of their takes alone, completely apart from the competence of the radio hosts themselves.

I don't typically go to Bills games. I went to the first football game ever played in the new Highmark Stadium when Buffalo took on the Carolina Panthers in the preseason, but I hadn't been in years prior to that and likely won't go again for a while.

But even I love the adventures that can only come from Bills tailgating. Throwing the football with strangers who become friends over some grilled food, irresponsibly jumping into tables, spraying ketchup and mustard all over yourself (for some reason I still haven't quite figured out)…it all makes for adventures and stories that people can tell each other for years to come. It's part of the quintessential Buffalo football experience. Other sports try it, other teams try it, but there's something special about it specifically for members of Bills Mafia. I smile every time the TV feed shows people who have obviously been tailgating for hours or ever days prior to the game, and I root for all y'all to have an excellent, yet safe, time.

Social media gameday traditions

Brother Bill (@TheeBrotherBill on Twitter) announced recently that his famous gameday morning opponent-specific videos (set to the tune of "Seven Nation Army" by the White Stripes) would be discontinued after seven years of providing laughs and coffee-beers to the member of Bills Mafia on social media, but other traditions remain. Greg Tompsett of Cover 1 (@GregTompsett) will still attempt to make the perfect steak the night before the game to "earn the right to win". His teammate Aaron Quinn (@AaronQuinn716) will still post his breakfast sandwiches. I will still type out the word "I hope the Bills win today" and post it every game day (I'll chuckle when I do it).

Traditions, even the tiniest ones, help create a shared community. And for Bills fans all over the globe who can't be physically in each other's presence like the tailgaters mentioned above, social media and websites like Buffalo Rumblings can help provide a venue for that community.

I love that football is back. But I love all the other little things that come alongside our beloved sport.

Let's do all of it together once again.

title: Christian Gonzalez signs historic new deal with Patriots
description: Christian Gonzalez has signed a four-year, $135 million contract extension with the New England Patriots, making him the highest-paid cornerback in NFL history.
fullText:
Christian Gonzalez has signed a four-year, $135 million contract extension with the New England Patriots, making him the highest-paid cornerback in NFL history.

NFL insider Jordan Schultz was the first to report the deal, which includes $102 million guaranteed.

Gonzalez's new contract is $3 million more than the deal signed by Seattle Seahawks cornerback Devon Witherspoon, who held the distinction of being the NFL's highest-paid cornerback after signing his extension last month. Gonzalez and Witherspoon share the same agent.

The massive contract comes as the Patriots get ready to open the NFL season on the road against the Seahawks in Seattle. New England will have Gonzalez on the field for the season opener, giving the Patriots one of their most important defensive players as they begin the new campaign.

Gonzalez celebrated the news on Instagram overnight, posting a photo with the caption, "Thank you Lord! PATS NATION LET'S GO."

The 24-year-old cornerback had been a full participant for most of Patriots training camp, but his contract situation remained one of the biggest questions surrounding the team throughout the summer. Gonzalez routinely faced questions from reporters about the status of negotiations as the two sides worked toward a new deal.

At the beginning of training camp, Patriots owner Robert Kraft said the team had offered Gonzalez a contract that would make him the highest-paid player at his position.

Before agreeing to the extension, Gonzalez was under contract with the Patriots for two more seasons and was scheduled to earn a little more than $20 million during that time. The new agreement instead makes him the centerpiece of a record-setting contract at the cornerback position.

Despite his importance to the defense, Gonzalez was not named among the Patriots' captains for this season. Still, his role on the field remains critical as New England prepares for a difficult opening matchup against Seattle.

The Seahawks have their own star cornerback in Witherspoon, creating an interesting backdrop for the season opener after Gonzalez surpassed him as the NFL's highest-paid player at the position.

title: Copley grad Landon Robinson begins Bengals career armed with powerful cause
description: Landon Robinson and his mother are in lockstep about the importance of the defensive tackle maximizing his ability to reach people as an NFL player.
fullText:
Landon Robinson called his mother with life-changing news last week while she was driving.

A Copley High School graduate, Robinson had just been told he made the Cincinnati Bengals 53-man roster, and the defensive tackle from the United States Naval Academy wanted to share the development with his proud mom, Patrice Robinson. But when the son and mother connected through FaceTime, it took a few seconds for Landon Robinson to spit out the positive update because tears of joy took control.

"I just really just let it all flow and really felt all the emotions of what just happened," Landon Robinson recently told the Beacon Journal by phone.

It's fitting for Robinson to reach out to his mom before anyone else. They are in lockstep about the importance of Robinson maximizing his platform as an NFL player and using it for the greater good. In April, they created the Landon Robinson Foundation, a mental health advocacy organization designed to address youth suicide.

"We don't want to waste that opportunity, for sure," Patrice Robinson, the CEO and co-founder of the Landon Robinson Foundation, said during a recent phone interview. "We want to make sure that we are able to help people just by being a light. I have a spirit and Landon has a spirit of jovialness. It's easy to be around us, and I love that. I think that's a gift from God, and I don't take it lightly."

More NFL news: Bengals select Landon Robinson in seventh round of draft

Robinson was born in Columbus, but his family moved to Fairlawn when he was in second grade. He attended Fort Island Primary School, Copley Fairlawn-Middle School and Copley High School, where he graduated in 2021.

Robinson, 23, and his mother said several high school students died by suicide during Robinson's time at Copley. Then a U.S. Naval Academy midshipman took his own life during Robinson's senior season at Navy. Shortly thereafter, Robinson started discussions with his mom about how he could impact the community in a powerful way. Brainstorming steered them toward mental health issues affecting young people.

"I've seen people struggle with mental health," Robinson said. "I've seen people make bad decisions with their mental health. Obviously, it's something that's uncomfortable to talk about, but it's something that truly needs advocacy and needs people to be speaking about it in order for it to get better.

"Even before I got drafted, my mom and I were just talking about, 'What's a way that we can help the community and we can help people?' We came up with this foundation, which is advocating for mental health and doing events to spread that wellness and just help people out in the long run."

As Patrice Robinson spoke on a panel in Rochester, New York, she gained a greater understanding about why some parents don't want to discuss youth suicide.

"There's a stigma that's attached to that. There's a shame that's attached to that," she said. "There are some people, which I was surprised to learn, but I learned that some people don't want to talk about it because they feel like it will plant the seed in their children to do it."

More NFL coverage: Nick Chubb's former Cleveland Browns teammates react to his retirement

The Robinsons aim to provide educational resources to families, and they have enlisted professionals who are qualified to spearhead the mission.

For example, Patrice Robinson's best friend, Arielle H. Sheftall, is the foundation's director of research and grant support. Landon Robinson calls Sheftall his "aunt" because of the Robinson family's close-knit relationship with Sheftall.

"Her research delved into the emotional side of things, the chemical brain makeup of these children, the social side, family, their environment and school and things of that nature," Patrice Robinson said. "... There was significant research that she did that showed that there are brain chemicals that shift at certain ages in a person's life and that when they're younger, they may exhibit some of these behaviors and some of these emotions, like depression or ADHD or so forth and so on, that if the parents could catch it young enough, they could change the trajectory of their child's life."

A reserve Marine, Landon Robinson graduated from the U.S. Naval Academy with a degree in cyber operations, and he is commissioned as a second lieutenant officer. He's well-rounded and realizes professional athletes carry a celebrity status. As an NFL player, he will likely be able to reach a larger audience than the average person.

"I've seen athletes have foundations and do things that can help people and all this stuff, but there were not too many people that really talk about the mental health side of things," said Robinson, who recalled Cavaliers legend Kevin Love speaking out on related issues.

In August, the Landon Robinson Foundation hosted a back-to-school movie night in Cincinnati. Monthly meetings with teenagers will begin later this month. Robinson envisions more community events, school visits and training sessions.

In the meantime, Robinson is preparing for his rookie season to begin in earnest. The Bengals are scheduled to open the upcoming season at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at 1 p.m. Sunday, Sept. 13.

Robinson's father, Lance Robinson, is a former Kent State University gymnast who grew up near Cincinnati and is a lifelong Bengals fan. Patrice Robinson said she started "screaming" and "crying" when her second of three sons revealed he had made an NFL roster.

A seventh-round draft pick (No. 226 overall), Robinson tied for first in sacks (four) and tied for second in pressures (10) in the NFL during the preseason, according to the statistics compiled by Pro Football Focus.

"I'm super excited to get started," Robinson said. "I think it's the beginning of a long, long career, and I'm just excited to learn and grow. Obviously, you want to get out there as soon as you can, and you're eager to go make plays, but it takes time in reality, especially as a younger player. You've got to learn and you've got to grow because it's a big jump from college to the NFL. So, I'm excited to learn. I'm excited to grow."

Cincinnati isn't the only part of the state waiting for Robinson's opportunity to arrive. His supporters in Northeast Ohio are eager, too.

"When my time comes to get out there and shine, then I'm going to take full grasp of it," Robinson said.

Off the field, Robinson will be able to pour himself into his foundation for however long his playing days last and beyond.

"Having something else that's greater than yourself is a great transition from a world that is full of glamor and lights and action," Patrice Robinson. "You have this other side of who you are, and that's what I try to tell Landon. It's like, 'You are a multifaceted person. You're not one-dimensional.'"

The Landon Robinson Foundation is proof.

If you or someone you know needs mental health resources and support, please call, text or chat with the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline or visit 988lifeline.org for 24/7 access to free and confidential services.

title: Who will reach Super Bowl? - NFL predictions for 2026 season
description: Who are favourites to reach the Super Bowl and who will be the surprise standouts? BBC's NFL experts make their predictions for the 2026 season - and so can you.
fullText:
The NFL is notoriously difficult to predict and last season was no different.

Seven of the eight division winners were different from 2024, with two of the Super Bowl favourites missing out on the play-offs entirely - the Baltimore Ravens and Kansas City Chiefs.

Two outsiders then made it all the way to the big game, with the Seattle Seahawks beating the New England Patriots for their first NFL championship in 12 years.

So, who will be this season's surprise package? Who will be playing at Super Bowl 61 next February? And who will be the main men?

Here, the BBC's NFL experts make their picks for the 2026 season, which begins this week. Plus you can predict your Super Bowl winner at the bottom of this page.

Rob Staton: I think the NFC will be another battle between the Los Angeles Rams and Seattle Seahawks. I'm going to go with the Rams, simply because only two teams have repeated since the turn of the century. I have them facing the Buffalo Bills. Josh Allen finally gets to the big game.

Hugh Ferris: You could argue that, aside from an underwhelming head coach hire, there's little reason the 2026 Bills will be any different to the recent incarnations. I'm picking them to finally get over the line, though, and reach the Super Bowl, but to lose nonetheless. It's incredibly difficult to choose anyone else rather than the Rams, isn't it?

Haydn Parry: Surely the Bills can convert Allen's talent and make it to the season showpiece? Joe Brady's promotion to head coach might prove to be the missing ingredient. From the NFC, I think the Rams look most likely to have a strong tilt this campaign, and I see them winning it.

Joe Bradshaw: The last time the Super Bowl was at SoFi Stadium in 2022, the Rams won on home territory and they look primed to repeat next February. From the AFC, surely Bills quarterback Allen is overdue a trip to the NFL's biggest game, even if it will ultimately end in defeat.

David Brindle: After losing Bo Nix to injury in last season's play-offs, I expect the Denver Broncos to use that as motivation and at least go one further this season. As for the Rams, it's very difficult to look past the consensus predictions for the Super Bowl.

Ben Collins: Full disclosure, I'd seen the above before writing this so here's some leftfield picks... imagine if it's the Los Angeles Chargers that actually get to play in the Super Bowl in their own stadium, and it's former Rams quarterback Jared Goff that leads Detroit to victory.

Rob Staton: I'm going with Josh Allen. He now has an offensive-minded head coach running the team. Everything will be geared towards him having a big season.

Hugh Ferris: In an attempt to think outside the box, I'm picking Justin Herbert of the Chargers. You might suggest a quarterback in a Jim Harbaugh team isn't likely to get the chance to have an MVP-level season, but the hiring of Mike McDaniel as offensive coordinator might change that.

Haydn Parry: I might be wearing my blue-star goggles here but Dak Prescott has the ability and the weapons to have an outstanding season. Offence was not the Dallas Cowboys' problem last year and it certainly wasn't Prescott's fault that the team failed to deliver. Dallas just need to find a 'D'.

Joe Bradshaw: Buffalo's new head coach Joe Brady has stepped up from offensive coordinator so knows how to get Josh Allen purring. If the Bills make the Super Bowl, their quarterback will be the obvious candidate for his second MVP award.

David Brindle: If it wasn't to be a quarterback, I fancy Jahmyr Gibbs. He's signed a new deal and now has no running back competition at Detroit so expect him to see lots of action on a Lions team who are NFC contenders.

Ben Collins: Cincinnati have remedied their defence and still have a top offence. After twice winning comeback player of the year, quarterback Joe Burrow stays fit long enough to bag the award he really wants as the Bengals make a deep play-off run.

Rob Staton: It could be Joe Brady if he can help Josh Allen reach MVP status, but in order to mix things up I'm going for DeMeco Ryans. The Houston Texans are going to lead on their defence and I think they'll be really strong.

Hugh Ferris: If the Bills reach the Super Bowl, then it stands to reason Joe Brady gets the nod as a first-year head coach, putting to shame people (like me) who called him an underwhelming hire.

Haydn Parry: I have always been a big fan of John Harbaugh. He will start from a comparatively low base in New York with the Giants, but with their passionate fanbase and the enormous potential of Jaxson Dart lift-off could be achieved early.

Joe Bradshaw: There has been such turnover on the NFL's coaching carousel, it has been hard to keep up this off-season. In the face of such instability, I'll opt for Sean McVay as he steers the Rams to their third Super Bowl title.

David Brindle: I'm going for Sean Payton to pick up his second award, 20 years after winning it with New Orleans. With the work done so far and decisions Payton has already made at Denver, this is the year I think it'll be formally recognised.

Ben Collins: After Detroit were hindered by a defensive injury crisis last season, Dan Campbell is rewarded as he gets the Lions roaring again.

Rob Staton: I'd expect Rueben Bain to have an immediate impact in Tampa Bay. Jadarian Price will get opportunities to shine in Seattle. I was a big fan of De'Zhaun Stribling, taken by the San Francisco 49ers. But in terms of pure impact, give me Caleb Downs, the safety in Dallas.

Hugh Ferris: The 49ers have one wide receiver AWOL, another out for the season, and injury question marks over Mike Evans and George Kittle - who's recovering from a torn Achilles - so along with a returning Deebo Samuel, there's a gap for De'Zhaun Stribling to fill.

Haydn Parry: It will be interesting to see how wide receiver Carnell Tate, fourth overall pick by Tennessee, adapts among the big boys. With his versatile skillset, the Titans expect him to contribute right from the off - the pre-draft scout reports highlighted his maturity, intelligence, sure hands and catch radius.

Joe Bradshaw: De'Zhaun Stribling was a surprise selection by the 49ers at the start of the second round but given their annual injury issues, he could be in line for plenty of work this season. Some fine displays in pre-season have only increased the hype.

David Brindle: After Kenneth Walker departed, the Seahawks picked Jadarian Price in the draft. He'll start the season as their lead back, with Zach Charbonnet still recovering from an ACL tear. I expect him to keep that job and become a top running back in the league for many years.

Ben Collins: Sonny Styles' athleticism caught the eye of NFL teams during the pre-draft process. He could have a big impact at linebacker for the Washington Commanders and soon become one of their leaders.

Rob Staton: I'm not suggesting the Las Vegas Raiders are going to go on an improbable run or anything, but Klint Kubiak did an excellent job in Seattle [as offensive coordinator] and should make the transition to head coach with ease. I think this will be the year, finally, that the Raiders show signs of growth.

Hugh Ferris: Here's a surprise: the New York teams won't both be terrible. The Jets' draft and John Harbaugh going to the Giants should mean they could rise to the heady heights of being mediocre.

Haydn Parry: Fernando Mendoza worked wonders at Indiana last year. He probably needs to perform miracles in Las Vegas but it will be fascinating to follow his progress. The lad needs broad shoulders to carry the weight of expectation but the Raiders can hardly do worse than last season.

Joe Bradshaw: Can you call a team with consecutive 11-win seasons a surprise package? Despite great regular seasons, the Los Angeles Chargers have faltered in the play-offs but they are now healthy again and new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel looks a perfect fit for talented quarterback Justin Herbert.

David Brindle: Given they missed the play-offs and went 6-11 last season, if the Cincinnati Bengals can stay healthy - especially quarterback Joe Burrow, who missed most of last season with turf toe - they could reach the Super Bowl and upset the status quo.

Ben Collins: Kevin Stefanski was twice named coach of the year at Cleveland and now has a more stable team at his disposal in Atlanta, led by dual-threat running back Bijan Robinson. If the Falcons can settle on a quarterback, they could finally get back in play-off contention.

Rob Staton: The Cleveland Browns are a shambles. The situation surrounding Deshaun Watson is a mess, and it's frankly incredible he's still in the league. They can no longer rely on Myles Garrett. They seem destined to fail.

Hugh Ferris: I picked the Browns last year and got it wrong. That won't stop me doing it again this year. They're going with Deshaun Watson as their starting quarterback, which will do little other than prove one more time that it might have been the worst trade (and contract) in NFL history.

Haydn Parry: There seems to be a general consensus that the Miami Dolphins are 'in transition' - which is NFL-speak for 'total rebuild'. They are probably in a race to the bottom with the Arizona Cardinals as things stand.

Joe Bradshaw: Iconic edge rusher Myles Garrett has left the Browns and they still have huge questions at quarterback with Deshaun Watson booed by his own fans during pre-season. Their best hope is a top pick in 2027's stacked-looking draft.

David Brindle: Until now, all of the questions have been tough, but this is easy. After a tumultuous off-season where they moved on from Jaylen Waddle and others, the rebuild is under way for the Miami Dolphins and they face a daunting season.

Ben Collins: Although I'm rooting for British tight end Seydou Traore in his rookie year, this could be a long season for the Dolphins. Their roster looks short on talent having also let Tua Tagovailoa and Tyreek Hill go, with Malik Willis entering a season as starting quarterback for the first time.

title: Browns 2027 NFL Mock Draft: Week 1 of CFB shakes things up
description: The first weekend of college football shook things up in our latest Browns mock draft.
fullText:
The 2027 NFL Draft will take place in Washington, D.C. next year. In that draft, the Browns still have their first-round picks, but a lot could happen in the next 8 months. Before then, though, there will be plenty of speculation and buildup about the team and who they may add through the draft in a class many are calling one of generational wealth.

While we will always look at mock drafts from analysts around the space, we will also keep up with our Mock Draft Mondays here on Browns Wire.

College football season is officially underway, so we are seeing some stocks fluctuate, and even some new players being added to watch lists. With that in mind and the stage set, let's dive into a 3-Round 2027 NFL Mock Draft for the Browns.

THE best wide receiver in the country doing what he does best. @Jermiah_Smith1 | #GoBucks pic.twitter.com/9iQKN9LRvQ

In the mock draft I did, the first three picks were Arch Manning, Dante Moore, and Darian Mensah. That took away all viable quarterback choices, so just like the actual NFL draft, I had to pivot. I could have gone with Dylan Stewart or Colin Simmons, but I instead went with the best player in the class: Jeremiah Smith. The Browns are loaded at wide receiver, but having Smith as a WR1, KC Concepcion, and Denzel Boston filling out the rest of the offense, it just makes sense. Jery Jeudy would be the odd man out, but that sorts itself out when his deal ends after the 2027 season.

Drake Lindsey looked very good in the opening week against Eastern Illinois. Now, they, of course, are not a defensive powerhouse, but Lindsey still made some NFL throws in that game. He showcased good decision-making, smooth mechanics, and good velocity on his passes to make tight windows. I like Lindsey a lot as an NFL Draft prospect from the summer, and it remains after Week 1 of the college football season as well.

You can put Minnesota LG Greg Johnson's name in ink for your 1st-round mocks. This is what a blue-chip guard prospect looks like pic.twitter.com/SSHFijbqx6

Greg Johnson looked very impressive, mauling defenders on the defensive front of Eastern Illinois in Week 1. He showcased his strength, movement ability, and awareness, all of which could easily have him in the first round of mock drafts. His falling due to position value to the beginning of day two of the draft isn't far-fetched, so the Browns land him here in this mock draft.

I made another pick here for the Browns, but after further review, I added another second to my thought process and went with John Henry Daley. In all seriousness, I like Henry Daley a lot as someone who can be a part of the rotation for the Browns' defensive front. He defends the run well, but that motor when he is rushing the passer is something else. He needs a pass rush plan, but coaching can teach that.

DJ's first big play for the Irish! 🔥#GoIrish☘️ | @DjMcKinney22 

📺: NBC pic.twitter.com/YqTgqQl8rG

I discussed it in the prospect preview for the Notre Dame-Wisconsin game, and he delivered. The Colorado transfer fit right in with the Fighting Irish secondary, and he benefited from the lack of targets that Leonard Moore got. He capped off a great game with a pick-six that took the game out of reach for Wisconsin, and they never recovered. He is someone who would fit right into the Browns' secondary and benefit the same way he does now at Leonard Moore by playing alongside Denzel Ward and Tyson Campbell.

title: Ole Miss QB Trinidad Chambliss just did what no FBS or NFL player has in 30 years
description: Trinidad Chambliss led Ole Miss to a clutch victory over Louisville, hitting a statistical milestone not seen in the NFL or FBS in 30 years.
fullText:
If there was any doubt about the upside of Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, his play in crunch time during Sunday's 41-38 win over Louisville quickly put it to rest. After Chambliss threw for less than 100 yards and lost a fumble in the first half, the Rebels still held a 10-6 lead heading into the break. However, it was the second half that put the college football world, and likely much of the NFL, on notice.

Chambliss threw for more than 250 yards over the final two quarters, tossed three touchdowns, two of which were 60-plus yard scores (both to Deuce Alexander) and tacked on a rushing touchdown. It was such a stellar performance that, statistically, it hasn't been done in a second half by an FBS or NFL player over the last 30 seasons, as Greg Harvey of OptaSTATS highlighted.

Trinidad Chambliss in the 2nd Half: 

-Multiple 60+ Yard Pass TD 
-Rush TD
-250+ Pass Yards

No other FBS/NFL player has done that in a second half of a single game over the last 30 seasons (including playoffs). pic.twitter.com/WYrvfd6uhy

As incredible as the unique history is, it's even more impressive considering the magnitude and timing of Chambliss' clutch plays. His first 62-yard touchdown came after Louisville took the lead in the third quarter, and the second one was after Louisville cut the Ole Miss lead to one point.

After Louisville tied the game just before the fourth quarter, Chambliss and Ole Miss responded in less than three minutes, as he tossed a 35-yard score to Caleb Odom to regain the lead. Minutes later, Chambliss scored on a five-yard run, which was followed by Louisville reeling off back-to-back scores to tie the game.

Finally, Chambliss led the Rebels on an eight-play, 40-yard drive in 1:28, including two 15-plus-yard passes to set up Ole Miss to make the game-winning field goal as time expired. Chambliss wrapped up the night with 336 passing yards, 60 rushing yards and four combined touchdowns on a national stage against a top-25 opponent. It's a stellar start for the signal-caller, who cemented himself as a legitimate Heisman Trophy candidate.

title: Ole Miss QB Trinidad Chambliss passes for 336 yards, runs for 60 in 41-38 win in opener
description: Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, who may prove to be among the most polarizing prospects in the 2027 NFL draft, is off to a good start to his final season of college football.
fullText:
Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, who may prove to be among the most polarizing prospects in the 2027 NFL draft, is off to a good start to his final season of college football.

Chambliss completed 21 of 36 passes for 336 yards, with three touchdowns and one interception, and also added nine carries for 60 yards and a rushing touchdown, as No. 9 Ole Miss beat No. 24 Louisville 41-38.

A year ago, Chambliss was a little-known transfer from Division II Ferris State who wasn't even expected to start at Ole Miss, but he became more than just a starter. He became one of the best players in the country, leading Ole Miss to the College Football Playoff.

So why is Chambliss polarizing as a prospect? He's on the smaller side (listed at 6-foot-1, possibly shorter) and is already 24 years old and in his sixth year of college football, so he may have less less upside and room for growth than some of the younger, less experienced quarterback projects.

Will Chambliss be a first-round pick? A Day Three pick? There's a wide range of potential outcomes, but he can help his case by continuing to play like he did against Louisville.

title: Chicago Bears legend Matt Suhey, best friend of late Walter Payton, dies at 68
description: Matt Suhey was a second-round pick who spent his entire 10-year NFL career in Chicago, mostly leading his Hall of Fame backfield mate to glory.
fullText:
Another member from the legendary 1985 Chicago Bears squad has passed.

Matt Suhey, the fullback and best friend of Hall of Famer Walter Payton, whom he so often led to daylight, died over Labor Day weekend. A person familiar with the situation confirmed Suhey's death to USA TODAY Sports. That person was granted anonymity due to the sensitivity of the matter.

Suhey, who spent his entire 10-year NFL career in Chicago, was 68. The cause of his death, which has not been publicly disclosed, is currently unknown.

"I felt like my dad and (Suhey) really got close because they had to be on the same page," Jarrett Payton, Walter's son, said in "A Football Life," an NFL Network docuseries.

"Matt watched my dad's back, kinda like being a bodyguard or protector. He blocked for him, he took a lotta hits, making sure that my dad would get the glory. Matt kinda sat back in the background, very unselfish."

Payton, who died in 1999, 12 years after he retired as the NFL's all-time leading rusher, was the godfather of Suhey's son, Scott.

A beloved teammate generally, Suhey also presented former Bears offensive tackle Jimbo Covert during his induction into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2021.

Payton, Suhey, Hall of Famer Steve McMichael and former safety Dave Duerson are among members from the famed '85 Bears, arguably the greatest single-season team in NFL history and one that crossed over into popular culture, who have died in recent years. Chicago made the playoffs in five of Suhey's 10 seasons, a span that has clearly marked the franchise's most sustained stretch of success during the Super Bowl era, which began in 1966.

A second-round pick out of Penn State in 1980, Suhey played in 148 games for the Bears and started 100 prior to his retirement following the 1989 season. He rushed for 2,946 yards and 20 touchdowns during his career, roughly what Payton routinely produced in two years.

But Suhey was also a very effective receiver out of the backfield, catching 260 balls for 2,113 yards, including five touchdowns and 93 first downs over the course of his career.

Suhey rushed for 52 yards and the first touchdown in the '85 Bears' Super Bowl 20 rout of the New England Patriots, still the only time the century-plus-old organization has hoisted a Lombardi Trophy. Infamously, Payton did not score in that 46-10 runaway, an admitted oversight by head coach Mike Ditka.

title: 5 NFL Teams That Will Let Fan Bases Down in Week 1
description: Every team has a clean slate right now, but of course, not all 32 NFL teams can start their season […]
fullText:
Every team has a clean slate right now, but of course, not all 32 NFL teams can start their season with a 1-0 record. While a Week 1 loss doesn't mean anything in the grand scheme of things, it's not how any team wants to begin the season. Yet, here are five NFL teams who will inevitably let their fan bases down in Week 1.

Whenever a team wins a Super Bowl, changes and new challenges follow into the next year. In this case, the Seattle Seahawks have lost their offensive playcaller, the Super Bowl LX MVP, and a Pro Bowl cornerback. While the front office is one of the best in business, including head coach Mike Macdonald, the Seahawks are also taking on a worthy opponent in the New England Patriots, who will be out for revenge. In other words, don't be surprised if the Seahawks start their season with a losing record.

Realizing last year's performance was nowhere near good enough, the Tennessee Titans cleaned house and surprisingly decided to move forward with a defensive-minded head coach. But what about Cam Ward's development? The No. 1 pick from 2025 finished with the third-lowest completion rate last season. While Ward may very well be poised to make a sizable second-year leap, these things tend to take time, building up over the course of a season. Ward may be improved, but it may take him some time to find his confidence, and the New York Jets are also playing with their backs against the wall as coach Aaron Glenn kicks off the year on the hot seat.

While the Green Bay Packers could prove to be Super Bowl contenders by the end of the season, the start of the year could get a bit rocky. Playing without two key starters, Josh Jacobs and Micah Parsons, the Packers will be relying on unproven players to fill sizable roles. Not to mention, they're facing off against a good and familiar opponent on the road against the Minnesota Vikings. Despite high expectations, the Packers' road could be bumpy to begin with.

John Harbaugh may be able to whip this New York Giants team into a playoff contender over the course of the season. Unfortunately, they get a pretty tough test in Week 1 against the Dallas Cowboys. Jaxson Dart is still unproven as a quarterback, and Malik Nabers likely won't be at 100% (if he's available at all), which will only place more stress on their second-year QB. Meanwhile, the Cowboys have one of the NFL's best offenses and a remade defense that has potential. The Giants should be able to keep this one competitive, but a Week 1 loss is not how any fan base wants to start the season.

The Kansas City Chiefs are flying a bit under the radar as the regular season approaches. That's likely exactly how Andy Reid, Patrick Mahomes, and Co. want it after missing out on the postseason in 2025. Yet, we know this team has potential, and they're extremely well-coached. Of course, so are the Denver Broncos. But the Chiefs not only have something to prove, they'll be working with home-field advantage too. It may be one of the few losses suffered by the Broncos all season, but a Week 1 wake-up call may be just what they need to kick off a Super Bowl campaign.

title: Clemson Tigers: Dabo Swinney Unsure About Starting QB After Week 1 Loss
description: The Clemson Tigers had a handful of question marks heading into the 2026 season, but none was as glaring as the quarterback position. fullText:
The Clemson Tigers had a handful of question marks heading into the 2026 season, but none was as glaring as the quarterback position. After seeing Cade Klubnik enter the 2026 NFL Draft, coach Dabo Swinney elected not to get a quarterback out of the NCAA Transfer Portal and instead kept his options in-house.

Christopher Vizzina was last season's backup quarterback, and incoming freshman Tait Reynolds was the other player vying for the starting quarterback position. However, it appears things can be rocky after just one game. Let's take a deeper dive into what Dabo Swinney had to say about Clemson's quarterbacks after Week 1.

Following the team's 51-10 loss to the LSU Tigers, there were a lot of questions about why this happened. Clemson's offense struggled passing the football as starting quarterback Christopher Vizzina completed 10 of 16 passes for 83 yards and an interception. Backup Tait Reynolds would also see some action, completing 4 of 6 passes for 22 yards. Following the game, coach Dabo Swinney was asked about who will be the starting quarterback for next week's game, and he responded with the following:

"I don't know. Again, we've got to watch the tape and evaluate and we'll go from there… That's what I said coming into it. That's why I said, we didn't want to guarantee (Reynolds) would play, but it was pretty likely he was going to play So we needed to play games. Again, I wish we had a game or two where you can work the kinks out, but thats not the stick we drew. We've got some stuff on tape now, we've got some things in real live games that we can evaluate, and we'll go from there."

Ahead of the game, it was clear the quarterback situation was something Dabo Swinney was still trying to figure out. He appeared on The Stephen A. Smith Show on Mad Dog Sports Radio and said the following about the quarterback battle:

"The quarterback is the big question. I mean, you know, and we're all gonna see it in real time. Chris [Vizzina] is gonna be our starter, and he earned the job and he won it, but we have another kid [Reynolds] that's right there. And we're just, Stephen A., as you know, we don't get preseason games. We're the only level of football from Pee Wee to NFL where you don't get to go and get some live preseason games. So our live preseason game is in Baton Rouge versus LSU. I've got confidence in these guys."

The starting quarterback situation between Chris Vizzina and Tait Reynolds is going to be something to keep an eye on throughout the season. It will be intriguing to see if one of them will be able to showcase their skills and take a firm grip on the Clemson Tigers' starting quarterback battle.

title: NFL rankings: Arizona Cardinals TE Trey McBride 26th in ESPN player rankings
description: A look at where Trey McBride lands in ESPN's projected top 100 players for 2026.
fullText:
The Arizona Cardinals have arguably the best tight end in the NFL in Trey McBride. He was ranked No. 13 in the "NFL Top 100 Players of 2026," the player-voted player rankings.

ESPN put together a list of the projected top 100 players of 2026. Where does McBride rank?

Even on a team with Marvin Harrison Jr. and Michael Wilson, it's not entirely inconceivable that McBride is the Cardinals' top receiving option. He spent the offseason refining his ability to read the defense and understand his spacing, which will only make the player with the most routes run in 2025 even more dangerous in space. Throughout training camp, McBride has put his receiving ability on display, a skill that will be amplified in new coach Mike LaFleur's West Coast scheme. -- Josh Weinfuss

title: ‘When You Drinking, Nothing Really Good Comes From It’ — Pro Bowler Reacts to Mark Sanchez’s Guilty Plea Plan in Stabbing Incident
description: Mark Sanchez’s legal saga took a significant turn last week when the former NFL quarterback and ex-Fox Sports analyst filed a motion to plead guilty to charges stemming from an October 2025 altercation with a truck driver in Indianapolis. Sanchez faced a felony battery charge and three misdemeanors, including public intoxication and unauthorized entry of a motor vehicle, after the alcohol-fueled confrontation left both him and 69-year-old Perry Tole seriously injured.
fullText:
Mark Sanchez's legal saga took a significant turn last week when the former NFL quarterback and ex-Fox Sports analyst filed a motion to plead guilty to charges stemming from an October 2025 altercation with a truck driver in Indianapolis.

Sanchez faced a felony battery charge and three misdemeanors, including public intoxication and unauthorized entry of a motor vehicle, after the alcohol-fueled confrontation left both him and 69-year-old Perry Tole seriously injured.

The guilty plea came just five days before his jury trial was set to begin, and former Pro Bowl wide receiver T.J. Houshmandzadeh, who has known Sanchez since he was a teenager, shared his reaction to the news.

Sanchez had been in Indianapolis to call the Raiders-Colts game for Fox on Oct. 5, 2025, when, in the early morning hours of Oct. 4, prosecutors say he accosted Tole in an alley between two downtown hotels while the truck driver was collecting used cooking oil.

The encounter escalated as Tole stabbed Sanchez in self-defense and was not charged, and both men were hospitalized. Fox Sports fired Sanchez in November and replaced him with Drew Brees.

The guilty plea, filed in Marion County Superior Court, requested that the judge vacate the Sept. 8 trial date and schedule a sentencing hearing. It remains unclear which specific charges Sanchez is pleading guilty to, and a judge still needs to formally accept the plea.

Houshmandzadeh, a former Cincinnati Bengals wideout who made the Pro Bowl in 2007, expressed sympathy for Sanchez while acknowledging alcohol's role in the incident.

"It's just unfortunate," Houshmandzadeh said. "It was an unfortunate situation for Mark because I've known Mark since he was a teenager… Great person. So when I saw this, I was like, 'Mark Sanchez did this?' It shocked me. And so, when you drinking, I guess nothing really good comes from it. And so the good thing is Mark is okay. The gentleman that he 'assaulted' is okay. At least I believe he's okay."

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

Houshmandzadeh also offered his take on the logic behind pleading guilty when the evidence is difficult to dispute.

"If it's on video, what am I pleading not guilty for?" he added. "You see it clear as day. You see pictures of the injuries, and so you don't want to have to relive that moment. Neither one of those guys want to have to relive that moment. Now, what does that entail, though, by me pleading guilty, what does that entail?"

"I got probation? Do I get community service?" Houshmandzadeh continued. "Because if it entails that I got to go to jail, and I've never really been in jail, oh, I'm not pleading guilty. I'm going to go ahead and press my luck. So, I would assume it's just going to be some probation, some things he's going to have to do community service-wise, and he'll do that no problem."

The plea deal appears to be part of a broader effort to resolve both the criminal and civil cases simultaneously. Tole has a pending civil lawsuit against Sanchez and Fox Sports, and his attorney Matt Golitko said the two sides are on "a positive path toward an agreement."

NFL insider Mike Florio noted recently that in cases like these, a civil settlement often shapes the criminal outcome, explaining that when a victim is "placated by, for example, a sizable settlement of the civil case," prosecutors are more likely to allow a plea that doesn't involve jail time.

Fox Sports has moved on with Brees in the analyst role alongside play-by-play voice Adam Amin, but the broadcasting world hasn't entirely closed its doors on Sanchez.

If the criminal case ends with probation and community service, and the civil suit reaches an amicable resolution, a return to television isn't out of the question. It won't be at Fox, at least not anytime soon, but Sanchez's decade of NFL experience and three years in the broadcasting booth give him a foundation to rebuild from once the off-field issues are put to rest.

title: What Lane Kiffin said about being hated after LSU’s 51-10 win over Clemson
description: LSU spent the week before its opener in a Louisiana courtroom and in an exchange of statements with the SEC over the eligibility of former NFL players on college rosters. fullText:
LSU spent the week before its opener in a Louisiana courtroom and in an exchange of statements with the SEC over the eligibility of former NFL players on college rosters. Lane Kiffin's first team then beat Clemson 51-10 in Baton Rouge on Saturday night, and he brought the argument up himself at halftime.

With LSU ahead 31-3 and holding a 336-54 edge in total yards at the break, Kiffin finished his interview with ESPN's Holly Rowe, started to walk away, then came back to the microphone and said, "Imagine if we had pro players."

Two days earlier, East Baton Rouge Parish Judge William Jorden granted a preliminary injunction barring the NCAA and the SEC from punishing schools that rostered any of the 42 athletes suing for a fifth season of eligibility, which cleared former Ole Miss players Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris to follow Kiffin to Baton Rouge. The SEC filed its own federal lawsuit against LSU and Kiffin in Alabama that same morning. LSU submitted a 103-man roster on Friday and left the two spots empty.

Kiffin explained that decision on ESPN's "College GameDay" hours before kickoff.

"That wasn't easy, as much as I feel for the players," he said. "And I believe that you fight for what you believe in. And I believe these kids have an opportunity to play, just like all the other kids around the country that are winning court cases and being put on rosters. But at the same time, I'm the head coach of LSU, and I had to make a decision that is for the big picture of LSU and the LSU football program, with the uncertainties of what potentially could have come by adding them to the roster."

"I'm just really glad they played the way they did, so that wouldn't have been the story, because I get it, it would have been the whole story," Kiffin said after the game. "Even if we won close, kind of ugly, the whole story would have been, man, I screwed the team up by doing this. I said it this morning, you can not agree with it. I've been criticized heavily for the last two weeks, and I get that."

Kiffin said someone asked him afterward if he had really put the halftime line on the air.

"What's the difference?" he answered. "Everybody hates you. They can't hate you much more."

Lane Kiffin, when asked about his halftime comments of “imagine if we had pro players”

Says someone asked him if he really said that..

Kiffin: “What’s the difference? Everybody hates you. They can’t hate you much more” pic.twitter.com/m4OwIOaxHI

— Trey Wallace (@TreyWallace) September 6, 2026

“Imagine if we had pro players.”

Lane Kiffin is not holding back. pic.twitter.com/OzHEZqw1UW

— ESPN (@espn) September 6, 2026

LSU ran for 213 yards before halftime against a Clemson team that finished the two quarters with minus-4 on the ground, and that gap is why the joke played as a joke. The 41-point margin was the worst loss of Dabo Swinney's tenure at Clemson and the program's worst since 2000.

Kiffin also pushed back on the idea that the week's noise reached his players, calling that talk overrated. The two roster spots remain open, and the SEC's federal case remains pending.

title: Ex-NFL agent: Giants RB Cam Skattebo's margin for error is shrinking
description: A former NFL agent believes the representatives of New York Giants RB Cam Skattebo must step in and save him from himself.
fullText:
The New York Giants are entering the 2026 NFL season with a running back room that has a little bit of everything. They have experience, depth, toughness, and versatility.

That is, if everyone can stay healthy and focused.

Which brings us to the case of second-year back Cam Skattebo, who became a folk hero last year in just eight games. Skattebo, a fourth-round pick out of Arizona State, suffered a fractured ankle midway through the season, but not before capturing the hearts and imagination of Giants fans.

His smashmouth style and straightforward approach to the game and life in general may not support a long NFL career. People are taking notice, most notably Giants' head coach John Harbaugh.

"Skatt's great. He does bring a lot of energy," Harbaugh said last week after Skattebo started a skirmish with defensive players at practice.

"But he did get a 15-yard penalty at the end of practice. Did you notice that? That's not infectious. Well, it is infectious, actually. Infectious in a bad way, right? Like an infectious disease type of thing (laughs). We don't want that. So, we want it to be directed in a positive way."

That's the issue. Skattebo has one speed. Full throttle. Joel Corry, a former NFL agent, believes Skattebo needs to be reined in. If the Giants won't do it, maybe his agent, or reps, should.

When situations like these arise, an agent should provide counsel to their client. It's an agent's job to tell a client what he needs to hear, not what he wants to hear. That isn't always done. Some agents are reluctant to be candid for fear of being fired and instead become enablers.

The initial backflip created an opportunity to warn Skattebo about the risk he was taking, considering he hadn't completely recovered from a serious injury. Had there been a major setback that jeopardized or ended Skattebo's 2026 season, which fortunately didn't occur with either backflip, he would have landed on the Reserve/Non-Football Injury list (NFI).

Corry is referring to the backflip Skattebo performed earlier this year at Fanatics Fest, where he didn't stick the landing. For a player who had not shown he could play football yet with his reconstructed ankle, this opened a lot of eyes. Not in a good way, either.

The Giants are aware they can't corral Skattebo completely. His persona is what it is. He's reckless in every direction he goes, so they had to go out and get themselves some insurance.

In free agency this year, they signed Pro Bowl fullback Patrick Ricard to lead the way out of the backfield. Ricard will take on the tacklers that Skattebo was taking head-on. It should free up some running room and spare Skattebo some wear and tear.

Then the Giants signed 232-pound Najee Harris to take early snaps and soften up the defense. That was Skattebo's job. Was.

Skattebo is talking about having a 2,000-yard season. That will happen maybe if he averages 20 yards per carry. His workload will be managed to the point where he might get anywhere from eight to 12 carries per game, max.

With Harris in tow and the team still very much aware that Tyrone Tracy Jr. is their only back with any measurable speed, Skattebo is in a committee situation with the Giants. Let's not leave out Devin Singletary, who is on the roster to provide a quick change-up a half-dozen times a game.

Skattebo may not want to pace himself and change, so the Giants could be quietly doing it for him.

title: Louisiana Judge Rules Players Can Go From NFL Back to College
description: The ruling allows players to go from the NFL to college rosters.
fullText:
LSU and Lane Kiffin are victorious—for now.

On Thursday evening in a courthouse in Baton Rouge, Judge William Jorden issued a ruling that extends legal protections for several football players seeking to go from the NFL preseason back to college rosters.

The ruling applies to dozens of players across multiple sports, and challenges the implementation of the NCAA's new age-based eligibility rule, rather than focusing on professional participation. It has sweeping implications, notably allowing players who have played in NFL preseason to sign with college rosters for the first time.

In the wake of the landmark decision, the most immediate question was whether some of the athletes in the case would appear in games—including Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris, who had signed NFL contracts but have since secured deals to play for LSU this season. LSU will have to make that choice, but has previously signalled they would roster these athletes if given the chance.

Those players are now protected by a court order.

The next question: whether the SEC and NCAA would be legally allowed to penalize LSU under the court's order. LSU is now protected, as Jorden entered a specification protecting the school from sanctions coming from the NCAA or SEC.

The case also raised an existential question: whether the SEC has the power as a conference to enforce its rules, especially in a legal environment where the NCAA is regularly sued. That last question wasn't answered by the ruling Thursday night.

The conference also filed a separate lawsuit of its own in Alabama federal court against LSU, Kiffin, and athletic director Verge Ausberry. With echoes of the Big 12's case against Texas Tech over Brendan Sorsby, the SEC is seeking a federal ruling that would ensure it could prevent LSU from playing these athletes.

The SEC is likely to continue proceedings in that case, especially if LSU rosters Harris and Wright for Saturday's game.

The landmark decision ends a contentious day in Baton Rouge, after several hours of oral arguments, including three hours of questioning for SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey, according to those present in the courtroom and reportedly left through a side door due to security concerns.

A web of elected officials either participated or looked on in person and from afar, including Louisiana attorney general Liz Murrill, who filed a brief in support of players and attended the proceedings. During the testimony, she singled out Dae'Quan Wright, saying, "Dae'Quan Wright, who played for Ole Miss, says he lost out on seven-figure NIL money in a fifth year. Mississippi didn't fight for him, but Louisiana will."

The legal battle didn't originate as one over former NFL players, however. The first Louisiana state case was one of many filed against the NCAA challenging the implementation of its new "age-based eligibility policy." The new rules allow players five seasons of eligibility—but the NCAA said it would not extend this new policy to players who started college in 2022 and had already exhausted four years of eligibility.

The players who filed the Louisiana suit were part of this group, but the case drew ire because some of the athletes had signed NFL contracts (even preseason deals) and been listed on NFL rosters. After Judge Jorden issued a temporary restraining order in favor of the players, LSU scooped up two of them: Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris.

In response, the SEC (as well as other conferences) released a policy banning players with NFL preseason experience. Neither the players nor LSU appeared to back down, however: Kiffin allowed Wright to join LSU practices earlier this week, while players' attorneys got the SEC added to the temporary restraining order.

Because of the SEC's lawsuit, the drama is likely only beginning. The case argues that the SEC would be harmed if LSU rosters players with NFL preseason experience or who signed NFL contracts, and asks a judge to "enter a preliminary and permanent injunction prohibiting Defendants from violating the Conference's First Amendment rights by compelling the Conference to associate with conduct that is contrary to the Conference's purpose and mission."

Attorneys for the SEC and/or NCAA are expected to file immediate appeals of Jorden's injunction in the hopes that it could be at least paused before Saturday.

LSU's roster for the season is due to be finalized on Friday. On Saturday, the Tigers will finally take the field against Clemson for the most highly anticipated team debut of the year.

Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry declared in a celebratory post on X/Twitter after the ruling: "Let's spot the ball! #GeauxTigers!"
